html:
On 12 November 1991 Indonesian troops opened fire on a crowd of young Timorese at the Santa Cruz cemetery in Dili, at a memorial for a student killed weeks before. About 250 people are thought to have died.

Unlike earlier killings, this one was filmed by a British cameraman, Max Stahl, and his footage was smuggled out and shown around the world.

It revived the cause of East Timor abroad. Solidarity groups grew, and in 1996 the Nobel Peace Prize went to Bishop Carlos Belo and José Ramos-Horta. Pressure on Suharto's regime grew until the vote of 1999. 12 November is now a national day.
